kjv: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God
mine: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ
note: SBLGNT follows Sinaiticus (first hand), Theta, 28 and Origen in omitting "huiou theou"; TR includes it (with Vaticanus, Bezae). The manuscripts are divided, and the phrase may have been lost by eye-skip over the abbreviated nomina sacra or added early.

kjv: As it is written in the prophets
mine: As it is written in Isaiah the prophet
note: TR "en tois prophetais" against "en to Esaia to prophete" in Sinaiticus, Vaticanus, Bezae; the composite citation (Mal 3:1 + Isa 40:3) was evidently "corrected" so as not to attribute Malachi to Isaiah.

kjv: And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand
mine: Moved with anger, he stretched out his hand
note: SBLGNT adopts orgistheis ("angered", Bezae and Old Latin) as the harder reading that scribes would soften, against splanchnistheis ("moved with compassion") in TR and most manuscripts; the choice is disputed. Context: anger (medium confidence). 1:43 'he sternly warned him and drove him out' shows strong emotion in the same scene; scribes are more likely to have softened anger than invented it.
